paper_of_the_week.title: Chondral Lesion Severity and Location Are Not Associated With Return-to-Play Outcomes After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
paper_of_the_week.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
paper_of_the_week.clinical_summary: This retrospective cohort study addresses Cartilage and joint health. The reported population was: concomitant chondral lesions and to determine whether lesion severity, location, or coexisting meniscal pathology influenced these outcomes The intervention or exposure was: primary ACL reconstruction with an arthroscopically confirmed chondral lesion were included and followed up for 5 years The direction and clinical magnitude of the findings are not reliably extractable.
paper_of_the_week.practitioner_takeaway: This study may meaningfully inform practice in Cartilage and joint health. The direction and clinical magnitude of the findings are not reliably extractable. Full-text review should still confirm the methods, intervention details, comparator, effect magnitude, adverse events, and applicability to the patient population.
paper_of_the_week.research_takeaway: Future studies should address the identified reporting and methodological limitations, particularly around effect estimates, precision, confounding, and clinical importance where applicable.
major_cautions: The retrospective design increases the risk of selection bias and incomplete data.
Retrospective data may contain selection bias, missing data, and uncontrolled confounding.
Clinical importance or a minimally important difference is not clearly discussed.

specialist_takeaways.sports_performance: The study is relevant to Return to sport. Sports-performance confidence is high. Transfer to competitive athletes depends on training status, intervention specificity, outcome validity, and similarity to real competition demands.
